chapter_title: Concerning the Fifteen Paths; and whether the Catechumen would have avoided causing his Wealth to go on the Three Paths to Gehenna
chapter_note: The oldest layer here is relatively compact: a systematic cosmological scheme of fifteen post-mortem “paths” in the zone, with a threefold “waste” discharge to gehennas, plus a mechanistic doctrine of “deeds/wealth” as detachable substances that can be freed from the places where they are bound and travel before/with/after the soul. Much of the chapter is a later institutional/pastoral graft focused on the catechumen/elect distinction, the apostle choosing “forms” of his church, seals of faith, and discipline (fasting/prayer/alms), consistent with the flagged redaction and the strong second-half pastoral drift; paragraph 8 is a classic editorial seam extending a cosmological scheme into church predestination language.

paragraphs.temporal_note: Formulaic dialogue frame: “Once again… elect… before the apostle… I beseech you, my master”. Hagiographic/instructional staging rather than impersonal cosmological exposition.

paragraphs.core_text: For we have heard thus from you: ‘Fifteen paths are drawn out in the zone. Four paths are pure and belong [to the] Light, leading up to life. Eight other paths are [mixed], leading above from that place. The Light shall go [u]p and become free through them; be purified and go in [to the] ships. However, the waste is separated and thrown [dow]n to transmigr[a]tion and the other three paths of [waste ...] discharged to the gehennas’.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Systematic numbered cosmological architecture (15 paths; 4/8/3 division) mapped entirely within the cosmic system (zone, Light, ships, transmigration, gehennas), with an impersonal explanatory voice.

paragraphs.core_text: You have explained [that the three] paths that belong to waste, the ones that are drawn to the gehennas, [a]re drawn from the fleshes. O[n]e of them is the appetite for [lawl]essness, that of people and of all flesh. The second is the [ ... ] all bodies, which is slaughter, [with] which all flesh is consumed. The third is the damaging action, which [ ... ] the Cross of Light and every body; together with the rest of the error and the blasphemy that wounds the gods.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Continues the schematic “path” taxonomy (three waste-paths) as a cosmic-mechanical discharge “drawn from the fleshes,” still inside the Manichaean cosmological system (Cross of Light; gods) rather than institutional exhortation.

paragraphs.core_text: Th[ese th]ree paths have you taught us, that they lead to the gehennas. And you have also [told] us that every person shall follow after hi[s] de[e]ds, whether to life or indeed to death.
paragraphs.temporal_note: General rule stated as impersonal cosmological law (deeds determine the route), still framed as teaching content rather than church discipline.
Petition/question addressed to “my master” focused on the catechumen and “faith of God”; this is dialogue scaffolding and institutional problem-setting, not substrate exposition.
Continues the question in a pastoral/institutional register (multitude of catechumens in the world; “faith of God”), functioning as narrative prompt rather than core cosmological mapping.
Dialogue attribution (“Then the apostle speaks…”) and reassurance formula; explicit ‘apostle’ marker is later compiling frame.

Editorial seam flagged: extends discussion into institutional predestination (“apostle… choose the forms of his entire church… elect or catechumens”)—cosmos→contemporary church identification rather than cosmos→cosmos mapping.
Institutional polemic and soteriology for catechumens (sects/heresies; seal of faith/knowledge; angels guiding deeds). This is church-facing application material.
Analogy deployed to support the catechumen ‘seal’ doctrine; embedded within institutional argument rather than independent cosmic mechanism teaching.
Catechumen-focused predestination (“form… chosen… in the heights”) tied to “mark of the faith” and ‘seal of truth’; institutional application dominates.
Explicit discipline and communal practice (fasting, prayer, alms to the saints) as institutional mechanisms; strong pastoral layer.

paragraphs.core_text: Immediately all his first deeds, that he did before he received the knowledge, shall be freed from every place wherein they are [bou]nd and snared. They shall loosen their bond and asce[n]d from heaven and earth, from the trees and the fleshes. They are loosened from every place wherein they are and go to the heights
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed institutional conversion markers and church rites that frame/trigger the mechanism ("right hand of peace", "rank of the true catechumenate", grace-belief language, and the clauses tying the ascent explicitly to "this first fasting and this first prayer" and calling them the "holy sign"), to isolate the older impersonal mechanics of deeds being bound in places and then loosed and ascending.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Within a catechumenate/ritual frame, a distinct older mechanistic substrate appears: deeds as quasi-substantial entities bound in cosmic locales (heaven/earth/trees/fleshes) that can be loosed and ascend—cosmos→cosmos process language.
Returns to catechumen-centered capability and exhortative implication (“has the ability… by his own hand”), in a pastoral/institutional voice rather than impersonal system description.

paragraphs.core_text: Now this matter is like this, the way [som]eone might dwell at a city, while his enti[re] following [is present] in the cities and the dwellings and the villages [of the country]. As long as, overall, the king is living in t[hat] place, you shall find his entire host living in those [dwelli]ngs that surround it. Also, whenever he may [give ... / ...] the sign for departure to the country, when he wishes [ ... ] to it, an indication is given by him to his entire follow[ing] so that he might set out on the road and depart [ ... ] each [pl]ace wherein it is. And he goes to the place where it i[s].
paragraphs.temporal_note: Impersonal correspondential analogy (king/host distributed through places; “sign for departure”) used to explain the mechanics of ‘deeds’ traveling; no explicit church institutions or NT overlay.

paragraphs.core_text: So, there are some among his expedition who shall travel before him and be prior to him. And there are others am[ong t]hem who shall wait for him and travel with him. They depart [at] his departure. Also, there are others among them who shall come after him, travelling behind him. They continue [very] many days and months travelling until they arrive.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Continues the structured, impersonal threefold sequence (before/with/after), consistent with older schematic teaching.

paragraphs.core_text: His entire following shall not depart a[t] a single time; but someone shall go first and another after him, while others shall depart with him.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Concise schematic recap of the before/with/after structure; no institutional anchoring.

paragraphs.core_text: There are some among his limbs and his deeds shall be puri[f]ied while he is set in the body. They are cleansed in [the] firmaments of the heavens and go before him. [Th]ere are some also among his limbs shall be freed wi[t]h him, at the time when he comes out from [h]is body. There are others shall be freed [af]ter him from the bonds of the earth and that of the creatures. [They] go and reach him in the land of the living.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed the explicit institutional application header: "This is also what the catechumen is like, with his deeds." The remaining lines present the older mechanistic schema (before/with/after) in cosmic terms (firmaments; bonds of earth; land of the living).
paragraphs.temporal_note: Underlying core mechanics are clear (deeds purified while in-body / freed at death / freed after, traveling through firmaments to the land of the living), but the catechumen-identification is a later pastoral application cue.
Concluding address in the teacher’s voice (“I have instructed you…”) about catechumen/limbs and angels; functions as editorial wrap-up rather than substrate exposition.
